name: Alternating Lateral Ball Slams
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a slam ball overhead with both hands.
Rotate slightly and slam the ball down hard on one side of your feet, bending your knees and hinging your hips.
Catch or pick the ball up under control and raise it overhead again.
Slam to the opposite side on the next rep, alternating.
cues: Hips and knees help the slam
longevityNotes: A strong, stable core protects the spine in every other movement and makes daily tasks — bending, twisting, reaching — safer. Core endurance matters more than core power.
overview: An explosive core and shoulder exercise that slams a medicine ball diagonally down to one side then the other.

commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back to pick up the ball
Standing too close so the ball bounces up into you
safetyNotes: Use a dead-weight slam ball, not a bouncy ball, and clear the space around you.
